summary: The note explains that the euro came into existence on 1 January 1999, though the goal of a common currency had been pursued by the European Union and its predecessors since the 1960s. It notes that the Maastricht Treaty, which entered into force in 1993, aimed to create an economic and monetary union by 1999 for all EU states except the United Kingdom and Denmark. The note is brief and covers only the origins of the currency.
one_line: Overview of the euro's origins: its 1999 introduction and the Maastricht Treaty's path to economic and monetary union.
key_facts: The euro came into existence on 1 January 1999.
The goal of a common currency had been pursued by the European Union and its predecessors since the 1960s.
Opposition from the United Kingdom was a major source of difficulty in the negotiations.
The Maastricht Treaty entered into force in 1993.
The Maastricht Treaty aimed to create an economic and monetary union by 1999.
The economic and monetary union was intended for all EU states except the United Kingdom and Denmark.
Denmark has a fixed exchange rate policy with the euro, despite being excluded from the economic and monetary union.
The negotiations toward the euro were described as tough.
